baseline: Host LTP 20260529 binary /nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin/epoll_ctl02 passes all 9 subtests on Linux 6.8.0-124-generic. Per assertion, the correct kernel returns: (1) epfd = -1, EPOLL_CTL_ADD -> EBADF; (2) fd is an O_DIRECTORY fd -> EPERM; (3) fd = -1 -> EBADF; (4) op = -1 -> EINVAL; (5) fd == epfd -> EINVAL; (6) event pointer NULL -> EFAULT; (7) EPOLL_CTL_DEL of an unregistered fd -> ENOENT; (8) EPOLL_CTL_MOD of an unregistered fd -> ENOENT; (9) EPOLL_CTL_ADD of an already-registered fd -> EEXIST. Two of those nine are broader rules than the test's single sample shows, measured directly on the host with a purpose-built probe: EPERM is not directory-specific but applies to every file whose f_op->poll is NULL -- a regular file, an O_DIRECTORY fd, /dev/null and /dev/zero all return EPERM, while a pipe end and /dev/ptmx are accepted; and the fd == epfd rule is an identity check on the struct file, not on the fd number -- EPOLL_CTL_ADD of dup(epfd) also returns EINVAL, whereas adding a *different* epoll fd succeeds, since epoll nesting is legal. A third measurement bounds the fix: poll() on a regular file and on an O_DIRECTORY fd both return revents=0x5 (POLLIN|POLLOUT), so a non-pollable file must still report itself unconditionally ready to poll/select even though epoll_ctl rejects it.
failing_assertion: Two of nine subtests fail, both because epoll_ctl returns success where an error is required (qemu.log:53 and qemu.log:56, from the selector boot at base e8f2b9ca6). epoll_ctl02.c:85: TFAIL: epoll_ctl(...) if fd does not support epoll succeeded -- expected EPERM (1), Asterinas returned 0 and registered the O_DIRECTORY fd in the interest list. epoll_ctl02.c:85: TFAIL: epoll_ctl(...) if fd is the same as epfd succeeded -- expected EINVAL (22), Asterinas returned 0 and added the epoll file to its own interest list. The other seven pass, so the run is 7 passed / 2 failed / 0 broken versus the host's 9 / 0 / 0.

impl.note: sys_epoll_ctl; the op match at 68-83 and the epfd resolution at 85-92 are the whole entry-level check set
EpollFile::control resolves the target fd at 72-74 and dispatches; add_interest at 87-128 checks only EEXIST
impl Pollable for InodeHandle -- the always-ready fallback that makes every inode look pollable

root_cause:
Two independent absent guards, both on the epoll_ctl entry path, and neither is a missing subsystem -- epoll itself works, since epoll_ctl01/03, epoll_create01/02, epoll_create1_01/02, epoll01, epoll_wait01/03/04/07 and epoll_pwait01/02/04/05/06 are already enabled in all.txt.

(1) EPERM. Nothing in the epoll path ever asks whether the target file supports polling; grep for EPERM across kernel/src/events/epoll/ and kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs returns nothing. Asterinas has no equivalent of Linux's file_can_poll, because Pollable::poll (kernel/src/process/signal/poll.rs:334-340) is a required method on the FileLike supertrait (kernel/src/fs/file/file_handle.rs:25), so every file is pollable by construction and there is no null f_op->poll to test. The concrete consequence is at kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:251-263: InodeHandle::poll delegates to the per-open file object when open_file is Some, and otherwise returns IoEvents::IN | IoEvents::OUT unconditionally, gated only on rights being non-empty (the O_PATH case, which yields NVAL). A directory opened O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY takes that fallback -- Inode::open defaults to None (kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:427-433) and the ext2/ramfs overrides only return Some for block and char devices -- so it reports itself readable and writable. sys_epoll_ctl therefore reaches EpollFile::control, add_interest finds no duplicate, and the entry is inserted, returning 0. The same fallback covers regular files, so Asterinas would also wrongly accept a regular file, which the test does not sample but the host probe shows Linux rejects with EPERM.

(2) EINVAL on fd == epfd. There is no self-add rejection anywhere: grep for 'epfd' under kernel/src/events/epoll/ returns nothing, and sys_epoll_ctl (kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:85-93) resolves epfd, downcasts it to EpollFile, and hands the target fd to control() without ever comparing the two. EpollFile implements Pollable via self.ready.poll (kernel/src/events/epoll/file.rs:255-259), so the epoll file is a legitimately pollable FileLike; add_interest inserts it into its own interest list and returns 0. Note that EntryKey (kernel/src/events/epoll/entry.rs:46-50) keys on (fd, KeyableWeak<dyn FileLike>) -- fd plus file identity -- which is the same pair Linux's ep_find uses, so the data structure already carries what a correct identity comparison needs; only the comparison is missing.
invariant:
Two rules, each stated without reference to the test.

(1) A file description that does not implement event polling cannot be registered in an epoll interest set: epoll_ctl(EPOLL_CTL_ADD/MOD/DEL) on such a target fails with EPERM. Pollability is a property of the file description's type, not of the inode type or of the fd, so it must hold identically for regular files, directories, and devices with no event source. This rule is independent of the weaker one the test samples: it is not "directories are rejected".

The rule has a companion that constrains any fix: a non-pollable file must still be usable with poll/select/ppoll, where it reports itself unconditionally ready (POLLIN|POLLOUT, i.e. Linux's DEFAULT_POLLMASK). So "declines epoll registration" and "reports no events" must be distinguishable -- a fix that makes a directory's poll return an empty mask would satisfy epoll_ctl02 and break poll() on directories and regular files, which is measurably wrong on the host.

(2) An epoll file cannot be added to its own interest set: epoll_ctl with a target file description identical to the epoll file description fails with EINVAL. The comparison is on file-description identity, not on the fd number, so it must also reject a dup() of the epoll fd. Adding a *different* epoll file remains legal, since epoll instances are pollable and nesting is supported.
owning_layer:
Both invariants belong above the filesystem, but at two different seams.

(1) EPERM: the per-open file description layer, expressed as a capability query on FileLike / Pollable in kernel/src/fs/file/file_handle.rs and kernel/src/process/signal/poll.rs, with the concrete answer supplied by InodeHandle in kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:251-263 (delegating to PerOpenFileOps when present). Asterinas's abstractions do not line up with Linux's here and it is worth being explicit: Linux gets this for free because f_op->poll is a nullable function pointer, whereas Pollable::poll is a required trait method, so no null state exists to test. The closest equivalent is therefore a new explicit predicate on the file description -- something like a `supports_epoll`/`can_poll` method on FileLike defaulting to true, overridden to false by InodeHandle when it has no per-open file object (and by any PerOpenFileOps that is likewise event-free) -- rather than an inode-type check. An InodeType::Dir test inside the epoll code would pass this test and still leave regular files and /dev/null wrongly acceptable, which is exactly the failure mode this field exists to prevent. Enforcement is then a single call from the epoll_ctl entry path; the check must NOT be pushed down into ext2/exfat/ramfs, or each filesystem would have to re-derive it.

(2) EINVAL on self-add: the syscall entry layer, kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs::sys_epoll_ctl, or equivalently the top of EpollFile::control in kernel/src/events/epoll/file.rs:65-85. This is the only place that holds both Arc<dyn FileLike> handles at once and can compare their identity, which mirrors where Linux puts it. Doing it in add_interest alone would be wrong, since the rule applies to all three ops.
linux_reference: Read fs/eventpoll.c and include/linux/poll.h at v6.11 (fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.11). do_epoll_ctl (fs/eventpoll.c:2257-2405) enforces both rules in the syscall implementation, above VFS and above any filesystem, in this order: fdget(epfd) then fdget(fd) for -EBADF (2266-2275); then `error = -EPERM; if (!file_can_poll(tf.file)) goto error_tgt_fput;` (2277-2280); then `error = -EINVAL; if (f.file == tf.file || !is_file_epoll(f.file)) goto error_tgt_fput;` (2289-2292) -- note this is a struct file pointer comparison, which is why dup(epfd) is also rejected, and note it is checked *after* the EPERM check, so a non-pollable target reports EPERM even when other conditions also fail; then ep_find plus the per-op switch yielding -EEXIST / -ENOENT (2359-2390). EFAULT comes even earlier, in the syscall wrapper itself: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(epoll_ctl) does `if (ep_op_has_event(op) && copy_from_user(...)) return -EFAULT;` (2413-2422) before calling do_epoll_ctl -- which is why the EFAULT and the invalid-op EINVAL cases already pass in Asterinas, since read_val at kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:70 and 77 and the match arm at 82 sit in the same position. The pollability predicate is file_can_poll (include/linux/poll.h:75-78), literally `return file->f_op->poll;`. Its counterpart vfs_poll (include/linux/poll.h, same header) returns DEFAULT_POLLMASK = EPOLLIN|EPOLLOUT|EPOLLRDNORM|EPOLLWRNORM (poll.h:24) when f_op->poll is NULL -- so Linux deliberately separates "cannot be epoll-registered" from "has no events", which is the distinction the Asterinas fix has to reproduce and which the host probe confirms (poll() on a regular file and on a directory both return revents=0x5).
other_callers:
(1) EPERM: the epoll_ctl entry path is the only caller of the pollability predicate in Linux -- file_can_poll has exactly one use site in fs/eventpoll.c, so no other syscall observes this rule and the check itself is genuinely epoll-local. What is not epoll-local is the underlying fact being queried. If the predicate is instead implemented as an inode-type test inside the epoll code, then every non-pollable file description other than a directory stays wrongly acceptable: regular files on ext2, exfat, ramfs, procfs and overlayfs (all of which take the InodeHandle::poll fallback at inode_handle.rs:251-263 because Inode::open defaults to None), plus the char devices whose per-open object reports IN|OUT unconditionally -- /dev/null and /dev/zero via MemFile at kernel/src/device/mem/file.rs:92-97, both of which the host probe shows Linux rejects with EPERM. Placing the predicate on the file description makes all of those correct at once and gives ~30 Inode::open implementors a single place to opt out. Conversely, any change to InodeHandle::poll itself is reached by every poll/select/ppoll/epoll_wait caller in the kernel, which is why the fix must add a separate predicate rather than weaken the existing always-ready mask.

(2) EINVAL on self-add: sys_epoll_ctl (kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:93) is the only caller of EpollFile::control -- grep across kernel/src for `.control(`, `add_interest` and `EpollCtl::` finds no other user, the cgroupfs `self.control()` hits being an unrelated method. So the honest answer here is that nobody else reaches this defect, which makes a narrow check at the entry path defensible rather than merely convenient. The only internal caller of the neighbouring del_interest is EpollFile::pop_multi_ready (file.rs:232), which passes an entry already in the interest list and is unaffected.
suggested_direction:
Two small additive changes, no new subsystem.

(1) EPERM. Add a capability predicate to the file-description layer -- e.g. `fn supports_epoll(&self) -> bool { true }` on FileLike in kernel/src/fs/file/file_handle.rs, mirrored by a `supports_epoll`/`can_poll` on PerOpenFileOps in kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs. InodeHandle overrides it to return `self.open_file.as_ref().is_some_and(|f| f.supports_epoll())`, i.e. false whenever it falls through to the unconditional IN|OUT mask at inode_handle.rs:251-263, and MemFile (kernel/src/device/mem/file.rs) overrides it to false so /dev/null and /dev/zero match Linux. Leave Pollable::poll untouched so poll/select keep reporting POLLIN|POLLOUT for regular files and directories, which the host measurement requires. Enforce it once, in sys_epoll_ctl or at the top of EpollFile::control, for all three ops, returning EPERM.

(2) EINVAL on self-add. In sys_epoll_ctl (kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:85-93), after resolving the epfd file and before calling control, also resolve the target fd and reject when the two Arc<dyn FileLike> point at the same allocation (Arc::ptr_eq, matching Linux's `f.file == tf.file` pointer comparison so that dup(epfd) is caught too), returning EINVAL. Alternatively do it at the top of EpollFile::control, which already resolves the target file at file.rs:72-74 and has &self for the epoll file -- that placement avoids resolving the fd twice and keeps the rule in one spot for Add/Del/Mod. Do not compare fd numbers, and do not reject other epoll files: nesting a *different* epoll instance must keep working, as confirmed on the host.

Ordering matters for exact errno parity: check EBADF on both fds first, then EPERM, then the EINVAL identity check, matching do_epoll_ctl's order at fs/eventpoll.c:2266-2292. Note that Asterinas currently reads the user event (and so can return EFAULT) before resolving epfd, whereas Linux does the same in its syscall wrapper -- that ordering already matches and needs no change.

Worth flagging for verify: enabling this line also makes the two adjacent all.txt entries epoll_ctl04 and epoll_ctl05 more likely to pass, but they stay commented out and out of scope for this run.
